temperature_range: 50−125 °C for SnS using 2, 100−250 °C for SnS using 3
summary: The study describes the synthesis of N-heterocyclic stannylene (Sn(II)) and germylene (Ge(II)) precursors and their application in Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) of SnS and GeS. The precursors, including rac-N,N′-di-tert-butyl-2,3-dimethylenediamine and H2S, enable the deposition of SnS and GeS films at relatively low temperatures. The ALD process using precursor 2 (Sn(II) amidinate) allows for lower temperatures and higher growth rates compared to precursor 3 (Sn(II) amidinate). The films are uniform and conformal, even in high-aspect-ratio holes.
evidence: The text states that 'GeS or SnS can be deposited on substrates even at temperatures below 50 °C, while ALD of SnS from 3 becomes slow below substrate temperatures of 100 °C because of insufficient vapor pressure.' It also mentions that 'the growth rate of SnS film using 2 was higher than that using 3 by ca. 0.3 Å/cycle' and 'the ALD temperature window of the SnS film using 2 (50−125 °C) is lower than that of 3 (100−250 °C).'
